reading.body:
Microsoft operates a data center campus in Warren County as part of its larger West Des Moines footprint spanning three counties, but the company publishes no individual site capacity figures, only aggregate worldwide statistics covering 500+ data centers across 80+ Azure regions. The campus is one of 52 mapped facilities in Iowa, where only 2 operators have disclosed megawatt capacity to the public, making individual site power consumption unknowable from published sources.

The West Des Moines campus reportedly represents $1.5–2 billion in Microsoft investment and is planned to expand to at least six data centers, with a sixth facility codenamed Ruthenium in development, but these figures measure capital deployment, not electrical load or AI hosting capacity. No certification data for this specific Warren County location is published in the disclosed specifications.

Iowa's state total of published capacity is 18 MW across all disclosed facilities statewide, though this reflects extreme underreporting rather than actual deployment, since Microsoft alone operates multiple facilities here with no disclosed figures. This campus matters to AI infrastructure tracking as a major operator facility that is actively expanding, but its current and planned power consumption remain opaque.
